- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days < -0.30), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 10-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive days < -0.40), model underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (alternating +/–0.20), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average or use sentiment-weighted median of last 5 days.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., 3 consecutive days down >1.5%), model often fails to anticipate; add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast for next 3–5 days if sentiment is negative.
